rows.howThisWasRead: The delivered fixtures carry no AcroForm: finalizeOfficialForm flattens every widget into a /Form XObject named FlatWidget-<n> and invokes it from the page content stream under its own translation matrix. ROUTE_OPTIONS.measured: TESTED, NOT ACCEPTED, AND THE BUILDER IS RIGHT. The form's own printed line is 'I am requesting ONE of the following' followed by Pardon / Commutation of Sentence / Reprieve of Sentence / Remission of Fine - an exclusive election, not a checklist. The route obligation:track-only:ND:nd-regular-pardon is an application for a pardon, so the relief is already determined by the route and leaving it blank would ship a packet that does not say which of four statutory reliefs it seeks. The tick is drawn in the delivered bytes at the Pardon widget's own rect and nowhere else. The three off-route reliefs are declared with the statutory definitions that distinguish them, and I checked each against the source's own page 8: N.D.C.C. 12-55.1-01(1) commutation, (5) remission of fine, (6) reprieve, (4) pardon - all four quoted accurately. The guide tells the participant to confirm a pardon is what they want and warns them not to simply tick a different box on this copy. The remaining 51 checkboxes are facts about the applicant's own history - including the nine per-case 'Pardon Requested Yes/No' cells, which are the applicant's election of which cases to seek relief for and are correctly left blank alongside the empty case table.

A second-order exposure worth recording, though it is not a defect in these bytes: the nine OffenseRow cells are held back only by requires_explicit_mapping/sensitive_fact, and the fifteen ProsecutorDefenseRow, DispositionRow and EmployerRow cells only by a protect category. Those are second gates, not role gates - if either gate were relaxed for some future build, this form would attract participant data into them the same way.
crossChecks.item_18_judgement_the_builder_asked_to_b: The builder flagged the item 18 residence table as a judgement rather than a measurement and asked a reviewer to challenge it. Challenged, and the refusal is right. The printed heading is 'Start Date | End Date | Residence Address' under 'List Your Last Five Residences'. That cell does not hold an address; it holds one row of a dated residence history, which is a compound fact. The platform holds a current mailing address and no span for it. Writing it into a row would assert two things nobody supplied: an ordering convention the form never states (the form does not say whether row 1 is the newest or the oldest residence, and the two readings put the same value on opposite ends of a five-year history), and that the row belongs among the applicant's last five residences. On a form whose own instruction is that an incomplete application is RETURNED, a row carrying an address beside two empty date cells reads as finished and is not. The cost of the refusal is nil, because all five rows are carried to the participant as REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING with that reasoning printed in the guide. Had the platform held a dated address history this would be a different question; it does not.
crossChecks.source_fidelity_observations_confirmed: Both of the builder's source-fidelity observations reproduce exactly and neither is a packet defect. (1) The second and third 'Check All That Apply' lines on page 1 end in the word 'on' and expect a date, and the form provides no widget for either: the only three widgets in that block (y 495-545) are the three checkboxes themselves at x 52.68, and there is no text field anywhere near them. (2) The third line reads '(see question number 26)' and SFN 14859 (12-2020) ends at question 24 - confirmed by reading page 7, where question 24 is 'Complete this section only if you are reapplying...', which is plainly the question meant. The packet does not renumber the form, does not correct its printed text and does not repeat the wrong number as if it were right.
